summary: This note is a compiled overview of the television singing competition American Idol, covering its history across seasons, format changes, judges, sponsors, record deals, charity events, and the show's impact on music careers. It describes how the show began on Fox in 2002, how contestant selection and the weekly finals evolved, and how alumni such as Carrie Underwood, Kelly Clarkson and Fantasia achieved chart success. It also notes controversies such as the disputed voting result in the season that Kris Allen won.
one_line: Overview of the American Idol TV singing competition's seasons, format, judges, sponsors, record deals, and alumni success.
key_facts: American Idol debuted as a summer replacement show in June 2002 on the Fox network, co-hosted by Ryan Seacrest and Brian Dunkleman.
The fourteenth season premiered on January 7, 2015, with Ryan Seacrest returning as host.
Fantasia was crowned the winner over Diana DeGarmo, and her coronation single was "I Believe".
Hudson, who placed seventh, became the only Idol contestant so far to win both an Academy Award and a Grammy.
For the first five seasons, studio recordings were released as a compilation album, and all five reached the top ten in the Billboard 200.
Ford Motor Company and Coca-Cola were two of the first sponsors of American Idol in its first season, which cost around $10 million.
Season seven premiered on January 15, 2008, for a two-day, four-hour premiere.
The show's original three judges were Randy Jackson, Paula Abdul and Simon Cowell, and all three stayed on the panel for eight seasons.
Idol Gives Back, a charity event started in season six, has raised nearly $185 million in total.
On February 14, 2009, The Walt Disney Company debuted "The American Idol Experience" at Disney's Hollywood Studios; the attraction closed on August 30, 2014.
Season 12 premiered on January 16, 2013, with a judging panel of Randy Jackson, Mariah Carey, Keith Urban and Nicki Minaj.
In May 2005, Carrie Underwood was announced the winner, with Bice the runner-up.
According to Billboard, in its first ten years Idol had spawned 345 Billboard chart-toppers.
Nick Fradiani won the season over Clark Beckham and became the first winner from the Northeast region.
Kris Allen won over Adam Lambert in the most controversial voting result since season two, with a later-retracted claim that 38 million of 100 million votes came from Arkansas.
